minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted a special permit for a ground solar array 15 feet from the side line, with a buffer condition.
minutes.summary: The board heard one application: Richard Conte's request for a special permit for a small-scale ground-mounted solar array at 355 Northfield Road that would not meet the 25-foot side yard setback. Neighbors spoke in support or without objection and asked about screening. A motion to approve with a solid fence and pine trees as a buffer was made, and the chair declared it passed.

public_comment.topic: No opposition to the plan as filed; wants notice and a chance to be heard if it changes; asked about boulders and vegetation affecting the array and about the earlier tree-removal permission.
No objection; called it the best location on the lot and urged the board to get the other abutter's opinion.
In favor; asked for the side-line dimensions and for deer-resistant vegetation along the line.
A resident asked whether the applicant could go back to a rooftop plan if this were denied; the board said a roof system could be built by right.

votes.motion: Approve the special permit for the ground-mounted solar array with a condition of a solid fence and pine trees on the line with the abutters as a buffer.

decisions.decision: Special permit granted, subject to compliance with all applicable licenses and regulations and periodic review; must be recorded at the Registry of Deeds, and lapses in two years unless construction has commenced.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a special permit for a ground-mounted solar array that would not meet the 25-foot side yard setback.
Approval carries a condition of a solid fence and pine trees on the line with the abutters as a buffer.
The permit is subject to applicable licenses and regulations and periodic review, must be recorded at the Registry of Deeds, and lapses in two years unless construction begins.
Abutters spoke in support or without objection, asking about screening, deer-resistant plantings and notice if the plan changes.
A resident asked about a rooftop fallback; the board said a roof system could be built by right.

why_it_matters: The decision shows how a setback exception for home solar is weighed: the board allowed a closer side line in exchange for a screening condition protecting neighbors.
The permit lapses if construction does not start within two years, so the array is not guaranteed to be built.
